transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I’ve been having these episodes where I eat a really large amount of food in one sitting, way more than feels normal. It’s starting to scare me because it feels like it’s getting worse, and I don’t really understand why I’m doing it.

After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever try to compensate in any way, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively to get rid of the calories?
No, I don’t usually do anything like that afterward. I don’t make myself vomit or use laxatives or anything extreme; I just kind of sit with it and feel bad, but I don’t try to “undo” it.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating, and do they happen at least once a week and cause you significant distress or problems in your life?

Yeah, during those episodes I definitely feel like I’ve lost control, like I can’t stop even when I’m uncomfortably full. They’ve been happening at least once a week for over a year now, and afterward I feel really disgusted with myself and guilty, and it’s starting to affect my mood and how I see myself.
Outside of these binge episodes, do you generally follow strict diets, skip meals, or severely restrict what you eat, or is your eating between episodes relatively typical for you?

Between episodes my eating is more or less “normal” for me—I’m not on any strict diet. I don’t usually skip a lot of meals or severely restrict; I just try to eat reasonably, though I’m probably more careful after a binge for a day or so.

How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself overall—for example, would you say they are the main way you judge your self-worth, or just one part among many things that matter to you?

I’d say my weight and body shape are a pretty big part of how I feel about myself, maybe more than they should be. They’re not the only thing that matters—I care about my work and relationships too—but if I’m unhappy with my body, it kind of overshadows everything else.
Has your doctor ever told you that your weight is in an underweight range or that they’re concerned you might not be eating enough overall, outside of the binge episodes?
No, I’ve never been told I’m underweight. No doctor has said they’re worried I’m not eating enough overall.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was F50.8 (other eating disorders). The history now clearly describes recurrent episodes of eating objectively large amounts of food, with loss of control, at least weekly for over a year, significant distress, no regular compensatory behaviors, no marked dietary restriction between episodes, and no underweight. This pattern is most consistent with a binge‑type eating disorder without compensatory behaviors. In ICD-10 there is no specific separate code for this presentation, so it typically falls under F50.8, but F50.9 (unspecified eating disorder) is also kept on the list because the exact ICD-10 categorization can vary depending on local coding practices and whether criteria are fully met/documented. There is no evidence for other conditions like those involving underweight, extreme restriction, or regular purging, so other eating-disorder codes are not included. The candidate list is thus expanded from [F50.8] to [F50.8, F50.9] to reflect this diagnostic uncertainty in coding rather than in the clinical picture.
